newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CVRD Q1 iron sales up vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CVRD Q1 iron sales up vs yr ago.

text.p: Brazil's Companhia Vale do Rio Doce sold 25.74 million tonnes of iron ore and pellets in the first quarter versus 24.91 million tonnes in the same period last year, a company official said on Monday.

Anastacio Ulbadino Fernandes Filho, the state-owned mining company's finance director and vice president, said CVRD's goal was to sell 105 million tonnes this year, up from 103 million tonnes in 1996 and equal to 1995.
"We foresee this year reaching the same level as in 1995," Fernandes told reporters.

He said first-quarter financial results for the firm, which is slated to be privatized on April 29, were not yet available. CVRD's physical iron sales declined in 1996 due to slimmer placements in Europe, which trimmed its buying of iron and pellets in favor of increased purchases of steel, Fernandes said.

The company's top market is Asia, principally Japan, followed by Brazil and Europe. Iron sales accounted for 38 percent of CVRD's consolidated gross receipts of 5.091 billion reais last year compared with 37 percent of 5.418 billion reais in gross receipts the prior year.
Fernandes said the price of iron remained stable at about $17 per tonne. Export prices could rise by 1.1 percent this year, depending on the world steel-price cycle, he said.
Gold sales at CVRD reached 3.6 tonnes in the first quarter, about the same as the first three months of 1996.
The company expects gold sales in 1997 to be little changed from last year's sales of 18 tonnes. It expects to place 100 percent of the 1997 sales on international markets.

CVRD expects to transport 62 million tonnes of iron for other companies this year, compared with 60 million tonnes in 1996, Fernandes said. In first quarter of 1997, the company transported 14.5 million tonnes compared with 14.9 million tonnes in the same period last year, he said.
The company posted net profit of 632 million reais in 1996 compared with 359 million reais in 1995, with profit boosted by improved efficiency, lower costs and higher revenue.
Fernandes said CVRD was comfortable with its debt position. Total debts dropped from $2.7 billion in 1987 to less than $1.0 billion in 1994 before rising last year to more than $1.5 billion.

He also said he did not see any snags arising ahead of the sale of at least 40 percent of the company's capital stock later this month despite concern that pensions funds holding up to 16 percent of CVRD may opt to sell shares at the auction.
